Synopsis:
Nightsong speaks with Shadowheart about Shadowheart's parents, causing Shadowheart to remember the truth. Shadowheart reflects that she needs to recover her memories in Baldur's Gate. Nightsong gives Shadowheart an artifact and a blessing.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_NightsongShadowheartVisit_CFM.json: Shadowheart is speaking with Nightsong shortly after Nightsong was freed from the Shadowfell and after Shadowheart suffered Shar’s wrath; Nightsong notes Shadowheart’s altered appearance and says she must repay a debt. Off‑screen, the player and Shadowheart previously liberated Nightsong, creating the obligation that motivates Nightsong to reveal suppressed truths and offer aid. Shadowheart’s memories were damaged or erased by Shar’s followers who raised and trained her, and Nightsong reveals those “adoptive” captors have in fact held Shadowheart’s true parents for decades — their lair and answers lie in Baldur’s Gate. To help, Nightsong restores some memories, bestows a Selûne‑tinged blessing and hands over the Spear of Night (an artifact once used by Shar but now mirrored by Selûne), warning that confronting the abductors will be dangerous.
- LOW_SharGrotto_ParentsFate_OM_Shadowheart_COM.json: Shadowheart meets with her parents once again, who have been imprisoned for decades. A vision of Shar appears and demands Shadowheart sacrifice her parents.Note: there are two major tracks in this scene - if SH comes to it as a loyal Sharran who is intent on taking control of the church at her goddess's command, or as someone who has turned from Shar and is coming to rescue her parents.
- LOW_SharGrotto_ParentsFate_OM_Shadowheart_AOM_OOM.json: Avatar Shadowheart meets with her parents once again, who have been imprisoned for decades. A vision of Shar appears and demands Shadowheart sacrifice her parents.Note: there are two major tracks in this scene - if SH comes to it as a loyal Sharran who is intent on taking control of the church at her goddess's command, or as someone who has turned from Shar and is coming to rescue her parents.
- FOR_Village_OM_ShadowHeart_COM_PostEA.json: POST EA DIALOG OF FOR_Village_OM_ShadowHeart_COMAfter finding Sharran crown on a skeleton, an old journal speaking of local disappearances or a defiled statue of Selune, Shadowheart recognises that the ruined village of Moonhaven was attacked by Shar worshippers at some point and realises she may have allies nearby. While she's contemplating this, she experiences a flicker of strange magic. Her companions may notice this and ask what's the matter - she can be truthful or not, knowing that leading the party to a Shar stronghold could end in the deaths of some companions.
- CAMP_Shadowheart_DreamReflection_SD.json: Shadowheart reflects on Shar and her own purpose while thinking back about the past.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Nightsong: It is time we spoke about your heritage. There is a debt I must repay. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: NS cocks her head as she looks at SH in curiosity, taking in her altered appearance post-Shar's wrath. (node 122)
- Shadowheart: You claimed to know something about me - you knew about the wolves. Tell me everything. (node 68)
- Nightsong: There is nothing I can tell you that you do not already know yourself. They trained you well, trained you hard. Chiselled away any part of you that did not fit their plan. They made you forget. (node 126)
- Nightsong: Shar's embrace is something that was forced upon you. It is not your true nature. (node 48)
- Nightsong: The natural conclusion is that you are no true Sharran, and never were. (node 88)
- Shadowheart: That can't be. I was always loyal to Shar. (node 172)
- Nightsong: ...Until you weren't. Do you think it was but a brief lapse? A moment of madness? No. I think you finally listened to your heart. (node 97)
- Nightsong: When you freed me from the Shadowfell, you severed a bond between me and that dog, Thorm. A bond of pain - his, inflicted on me. (node 106)
- Nightsong: When I laid eyes on you, I sensed a similar bond. You, tethered to two others, someplace distant. (node 5)
- Nightsong: Let me help you remember so there will be no doubt. (node 120)
- Narrator: *A memory appears at the forefront of your mind.* (node 82)
- : True (node 128)
- Narrator: *You remember that it is a common rite amongst Selûne's followers to send their children off into the woods to find their way home. Perhaps this time it had gone awry.* (node 96)
- Shadowheart: That wolf - that elf... Who was he? (node 7)
- Nightsong: You already know who he is. Did you not see yourself in him? Do you not recognise your own blood? (node 83)
- Nightsong: He is your father - and he lives still, as does your mother. I felt them, bound to you. (node 14)
- Shadowheart: That can't be. I'm an orphan. (node 27)
- Nightsong: And who told you that? Your adoptive family? You are not to blame. You were young, impressionable. They took you because they wanted to break and remake you. (node 61)
- Nightsong: But you are a child no longer. You are a woman. One who knows what must be done. (node 175)
- Shadowheart: I have to find my parents. (node 85)
- Nightsong: You will have to face your abductors in their very lair, in Baldur's Gate. (node 185)
- Nightsong: You may have once thought of them as comrades, mentors, friends, even lovers. But they will all be enemies now. (node 13)
- Nightsong: There is one more way in which I can help you. You have been forewarned, and now you shall be forearmed. (node 131)
- Nightsong: You will remember this spear, no doubt? It was to be the instrument of my death. Now it will become a parting gift in exchange for my life. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Nightsong produces the Spear of Night, holding it in both hands. (node 59)
- Shadowheart: Shar's weapon? Surely it's useless now. (node 115)
- Nightsong: For her purposes, perhaps. Shar is quick to discard whatever she has no use for. I think you know that well enough. (node 116)
- Nightsong: I felt the Spear call to me as I took flight. Whatever Shar calls her own, Selûne has equal claim to. They are one and the same. Their power is matched... (node 21)
- Nightsong: ...and mirrored. Take it - you will need it. But what you do with it... that will be up to you. Same as before. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Nightsong sweeps her palm down the length of the spear. It glows with ethereal selunite power. (node 80)
- Shadowheart: Thank you. (node 33)
- Nightsong: A debt repaid. You gave me my life back. Now go and claim your own. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Nightsong mimes handing over the spear to Avatar SH, who puts it away. (node 67)
- Nightsong: I have kept my word. My guidance in exchange for my freedom. (node 178)
- Shadowheart: There must be more you can tell me. (node 43)
- Nightsong: Your mind is a deep, dark wood. There are dead ends, shadowy corners, lurking threats. I was lucky to be able to glean as much as I did. (node 41)
- Nightsong: Besides, there are more hardships ahead. Knowing too much may cause you to despair, while a little ignorance may shield you. (node 51)
- Nightsong: One last thing: your parents have been in the hands of Shar's followers for some forty years. It must take tremendous will for mortals to hold out that long. (node 52)
- Nightsong: See that their sacrifices are not in vain: allow the Moonmaiden to guide you at last. (node 153)
- Narrator: *She speaks pure heresy, or so you would have once thought. But you can deny it no longer - a new presence empowers you. You felt it ever since the Shadowfell. Selûne.* (node 71)

context: Nightsong is speaking to Shadowheart shortly after the player and Shadowheart liberated her from the Shadowfell; Nightsong feels indebted because the rescue severed a painful bond she shared with a creature named Thorm and she now repays that debt. Shadowheart has recently suffered Shar’s wrath and bears altered scars and damaged memories—she was raised and brutally trained by Shar’s followers who told her she was an orphan and erased much of her past. Nightsong reveals that Shadowheart’s true parents are alive but have been held by those followers for decades, that pieces of memory can be restored, and that their lair and answers lie in Baldur’s Gate. To help, Nightsong bestows a Selûne‑tinged blessing and gives Shadowheart the Spear of Night (an artifact tied to Shar but now mirrored by Selûne), while warning that confronting her abductors will be dangerous and that some truths must remain guarded.
